subject: Slate snapshot & slate-split plan for Q3 pilot — ops + product alignment
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@acmehealth.com>, CloudX Ops <ops@cloudx.io>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Slate snapshot & slate-split plan for Q3 pilot — ops + product alignment

Quick summary: Acme's Q3 pilot needs a temporary re-slice of their Dedicated pool to run both a low-latency inference lane (interactive chat) and a separate batch sweep for nightly model calibrations. They asked for a carveout we can guarantee between Mar 15–Jun 30.

Ask to the group: can we create a temporary split of their reserved GPU slice into: (A) 20% low-latency lane (p99 target 200ms), (B) 40% batch lane (higher throughput, tolerant latency), and (C) remaining shared buffer for autoscale/overflow? Acrobatics: this will require an autoscaling-policy exception (allowing burst beyond their reserved commit into dedicated buffer for 2 hours/night), plus a short SLA change while the slice exists.

I attached a quick snapshot of the pilot forecast and a proposal for the split. High-level product questions below that I need help answering before I reply to Acme: 1) Can product sign off on temporary p99 target widening for the batch lane? 2) Ops — do we have a documented runbook for temporary slice splitting + rollback? 3) Sales (Laura) — are there commercial concerns about billing during the carveout window?

Next step: I propose a 30-minute sync Wed Mar 3 to lock numbers so I can send a formal carveout confirmation to Acme by Thu EOD.

Attachments: q3_slate_snapshot_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), pool-split-proposal.pdf (proposal)

Thanks,
Jonas
Director, Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Slate snapshot & slate-split plan for Q3 pilot — ops + product alignment

Jonas — thanks for the clear ask and the proposal. A few quick product points: 1) We're okay with widening the p99 target for the batch lane to 800ms provided we put a hard gating rule in the routing policy so interactive traffic stays pinned to the low-latency lane. 2) We should require canary verification for model quality post-split — schedule a small traffic ramp for day 1. 3) For the autoscale exception, product prefers a time-bounded policy (e.g., daily 2-hour burst window) and telemetry signals that trigger automatic rollback.

I'll be on the sync Wed — please add an agenda item for canary metrics and rollback thresholds. Also, Marcus and ops, if this split changes placement constraints (GPU type mixing) call it out so we can adjust kernel selection profiles.

-Kimberly
VP, Product
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, CloudX Ops <ops@cloudx.io>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Slate snapshot & slate-split plan for Q3 pilot — ops + product alignment

Appreciate the details. Ops feasibility notes: 1) We can implement a logical slice split within the dedicated pool (no physical reprovisioning) using our allocation shim — expected work: ~3–4 engineer-hours to add the temporary routing labels and a config change. 2) The autoscale exception is doable but needs QA: we'll add a rate limiter for burst windows and an emergency evict signal if buffer pressure > 85% for > 5min. 3) Runbook: I attached a draft (runbook_draft.md) with rollback steps and validation commands.

Risk: if Acme's batch jobs are heavy on memory, the kernel selection may fall back to less-optimized paths causing higher cost. We should explicitly list acceptable model size/sequence-length ranges in the carveout.

I'll plan to have the runbook updated and a canary checklist ready by Wed's sync.

-Marcus
Head of Infrastructure
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Slate snapshot & slate-split plan for Q3 pilot — ops + product alignment

Looping in Acme's PM (Alice) so expectations are clear. From a commercial perspective: the carveout should be treated as a temporary amendment to the Dedicated contract (no change to headline commitment, but a short addendum that clarifies billing for burst hours). We typically bill the reserved commit as-is and discount the burst-capacity consumption at 40% off list for pilot customers — proposal attached in pool-split-proposal.pdf.

Alice, can you confirm: 1) the nightly batch window you plan to use (start/end times and timezone), 2) whether the batch job can accept queued backpressure beyond a 10-min SLA, and 3) a single point of contact we can notify if we need an emergency eviction?

If all good, Jonas — this commercial approach should keep legal and finance out of the critical path.

-Laura
Enterprise Sales
From: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@acmehealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Slate snapshot & slate-split plan for Q3 pilot — ops + product alignment

Thanks everyone — this looks good and practical. Answers below: 1) Nightly batch window: 01:00–04:00 UTC (we run model sweeps and retraining batches then). 2) Batch backpressure: acceptable up to 20 minutes for non-critical recalibration jobs, but anything beyond that needs notification. 3) SPOC: me (alice.moreno@acmehealth.com) and on-call infra: infra-oncall@acmehealth.com.

We reviewed the billing approach in the proposal and are comfortable with the temporary addendum. Please send the formal carveout confirmation (dates Mar 15–Jun 30, lanes and burst window) and the canary checklist so we can schedule our validation run the first night.

Thanks — Alice
Product Manager, Acme Health
